# Load data

```{r}
#| label: Function to combine multiple datasets by species
#| include: false
multi_inner<- function(...){
  df1 = list(...)[[1]]
  df2 = list(...)[[2]]
  col1 = colnames(df1)[1]
  col2 = colnames(df2)[1]
  xxx = inner_join(..., by = "Species")
  return(xxx)
}
```

## Load tree and make ultrametric

```{r}
#| include: false
#load the tree
Flytree<-readNexus(file="../data/FlyTree_correctednames.3.0.nex")
is.ultrametric(Flytree)

#Why is the tree not ultrametric?
#After saving the tree to file, we lose some numerical precision, which can falsely cause the ultrametric tree to fail the is.ultrametric() test
ult.Flytree<-force.ultrametric(Flytree, method="nnls")
#Verify that it is ultrametric
is.ultrametric(ult.Flytree)
rm(Flytree)

```

## Make theme and data subset functions

**All traits show considerable variation among groups**

```{r}
#set theme for all density plots
# Define your custom theme and scales as an object
# 
colorscheme_9 = list(
  Zaprionus = "#57744C",
  Immigrans = "#6ac9ca",
  Virilis = "#4753a4",
  Repleta = "#692369",
  `Willistoni/Saltans` = "#3f5ba9",
  Obscura = "#c4d930",
  Melanogaster = "#fac9d4",
  Montium = "#a5c3db",
  `All species` = "grey50"
)

density_theme <- list(
  stat_density_ridges(
    aes(fill = Broad_clade),
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.5, panel_scaling = T,
    quantile_lines = F,
    scale = 0.6, linewidth = 0.2),
  scale_y_discrete("", expand = c(0, 0) ),
  scale_fill_manual("", values = colorscheme_9),
  theme_ridges(font_family = "Times", center_axis_labels = T, font_size = 10),
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 90,hjust = 0.5, size = 8),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.margin = margin(t = 25,r = 5,l = 5,b = 0, unit = "pt")
  )
)

make_df_for_density <- function(metric) {
  select_cols <- c("Species",
                   paste0(metric, "_f"),
                   paste0(metric, "_m"),
                   paste0(metric, "_sd")
                   )
  df_demographic_metrics<- df_demographic_metrics %>%
  dplyr::mutate(H_f = Keyfitz_Entropy_f,H_m = Keyfitz_Entropy_m, H_sd = Keyfitz_sd,
                G0_f = Lifespan_Gini_f, G0_m = Lifespan_Gini_m,G0_sd = G0_f -G0_m)
  
  df <- df_demographic_metrics %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(select_cols)) %>% #view()
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -c(Species),
      names_to = "Y",
      values_to = metric,
      names_prefix = paste0(metric, "_")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Y = case_when(
        Y == "f" ~ "Female (Days)",
        Y == "m" ~ "Male (Days)",
        Y == "sd" ~ "Sex-difference",
        .default = Y
      )
    ) %>%
    left_join(df_species_metadata %>%
                select(Species, Broad_clade)) %>%
    bind_rows(
      df_demographic_metrics %>%
        dplyr::select(all_of(select_cols)) %>% #view()
        pivot_longer(
          cols = -c(Species),
          names_to = "Y",
          values_to = metric,
          names_prefix = paste0(metric, "_")
        ) %>%
        mutate(
          Y = case_when(
            Y == "f" ~ "Female (Days)",
            Y == "m" ~ "Male (Days)",
            Y == "sd" ~ "Sex-difference",
            .default = Y
          ),
          Broad_clade = "All species"
        )
    ) %>%
    filter(Broad_clade != "Miscellaneous") %>%
    mutate(Broad_clade = factor(
      Broad_clade,
      levels = c(
        "All species",
        "Montium",
        "Melanogaster",
        "Obscura",
        "Willistoni/Saltans",
        "Repleta",
        "Virilis",
        "Immigrans",
        "Zaprionus"
      ),
      ordered = T
    ))
  return(df)
}

```
## Mortality metrics
### Ls50 (median lifespan): Female ls50 ranged from 2 -18 weeks. Male ls50 ranged from 1.5 – 17 weeks. Species (sex-average) ls50 ranged from 1.75 – 15 weeks. Sex-bias (log(female/male)) in LS50 ranged from highly female bias (1.18) to male biased (-0.75).

::: scrollable
```{r, fig.cap= "Density ridges of median lifespan (x-axis) by sex (facet) and broad clade.\nThe grey density plots show the overall distribution across all 148 species", message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=10}

df_plot_ls50 <- make_df_for_density("ls50")
p_ls50_density <- df_plot_ls50 %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = ls50, y = Broad_clade)) +
  density_theme+
  scale_x_continuous() +
  facet_wrap( ~ Y, ncol = 3, scales = "free_x", strip.position = "top") +
  facetted_pos_scales(
    x = list(
      Y == "Female (Days)" ~ scale_x_continuous(name = "Median lifespan",
                                                limits = c(0, 120), n.breaks = 3),
      Y == "Male (Days)"   ~ scale_x_continuous(name = "Median lifespan",
                                                limits = c(0, 120), n.breaks = 3),
      Y == "Sex-difference" ~ scale_x_continuous(name = "Median lifespan", n.breaks = 3) # Leaves this one truly free
    )
  ) 

#p_ls50_density

```
:::

## Shape metrics   
- Standardized aging rate : Standardized aging rate ranged from 0.53 - 9.39, 0.65 to 9.43, and 0.59 - 9.41 for females, males and average for species, respectively. Sex difference in aging rate ranged from 1.25 (higher aging rate in female) to (-1.17)

::: scrollable

Age at reproductive maturity

```{r}
p_repmat_density <- df_demographic_metrics %>%
  dplyr::select(Species, Age_reproductive_maturity_F, Age_reproductive_maturity_M) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Species),
    names_to = "Y",
    values_to = "Age at reproductive maturity",
    names_prefix = "Age_reproductive_maturity_"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Y = case_when(Y == "F" ~ "Female", Y == "M" ~ "Male", .default = "Species average")) %>%
  left_join(df_species_metadata %>% select(Species, Broad_clade), by = "Species") %>%
  filter(Broad_clade != "Miscellaneous") %>%
  bind_rows(
    df_demographic_metrics %>%
      dplyr::select(Species, Age_reproductive_maturity_F, Age_reproductive_maturity_M) %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = -c(Species),
        names_to = "Y",
        values_to = "Age at reproductive maturity",
        names_prefix = "Age_reproductive_maturity_"
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        Y = case_when(Y == "F" ~ "Female", Y == "M" ~ "Male", .default = "Species average")
      ) %>% mutate(Broad_clade = "All species")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = `Age at reproductive maturity`, y = Broad_clade)) +
  scale_x_continuous() +
  facet_wrap( ~ Y,
              scales = "free_x",
              ncol = 4,
              strip.position = "top") +
  density_theme

p_repmat_density

### Fecundity Metrics

Below is a cartoon depicting the relation between survival, age-specific fecundity, and fecundity scaled by survival and Net reproductive output (lifetime fecundity scaled by survival, i.e., area under the black curve):

![](data/Demo_cartoon.png){fig-align="center" width="351"}


::: scrollable
```{r, fig.cap= "Density ridges of Reproductive output(x-axis) by broad clade.\nThe grey density plots show the overall distribution across all 148 species Standardized early reproductive output values are in %. All other values are log transformed", message=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}


df_demographic_metrics %>%
  dplyr::select(Species,
                net_reproductive_output,
                Peak_Fecundity,
                Senescence_Slope,
                Shape_Rep) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(Species),
               names_to = "Y",
               values_to = "Reproductive output") %>%
  mutate(
    Y = case_when(
      Y == "net_reproductive_output" ~ "Net repro. output",
      Y == "Peak_Fecundity" ~ "Peak fecundity",
      Y == "Senescence_Slope" ~ "Repro. sen",
      Y == "Shape_Rep" ~ "Repro. shape"
    ),
    Y = factor(Y, levels = c(
      "Net repro. output", "Peak fecundity", "Repro. sen", "Repro. shape"
    ))
  ) %>%
  left_join(df_species_metadata %>% select(Species, Broad_clade)) %>%
  filter(Broad_clade != "Miscellaneous") %>%
  bind_rows(
    df_demographic_metrics %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Species,
        net_reproductive_output,
        Peak_Fecundity,
        Senescence_Slope,
        Shape_Rep
      ) %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = -c(Species),
        names_to = "Y",
        values_to = "Reproductive output"
      ) %>%
      mutate(
    Broad_clade = "All species",  
    Y = case_when(
      Y == "net_reproductive_output" ~ "Net repro. output",
      Y == "Peak_Fecundity" ~ "Peak fecundity",
      Y == "Senescence_Slope" ~ "Repro. sen",
      Y == "Shape_Rep" ~ "Repro. shape"
    ),
    Y = factor(Y, levels = c(
      "Net repro. output", "Peak fecundity", "Repro. sen", "Repro. shape"
    ))
  )
  )%>%
  mutate(Broad_clade = factor(
    Broad_clade,
    levels = c(
      "All species",
      "Montium",
      "Melanogaster",
      "Obscura",
      "Willistoni/Saltans",
      "Repleta",
      "Virilis",
      "Immigrans",
      "Zaprionus"
    ),
    ordered = T
  )) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = `Reproductive output` + 1, y = Broad_clade)) +
  facet_wrap( ~ Y,
              scales = "free_x",
              nrow = 1,
              strip.position = "top") +
  scale_x_log10("Reproductive output metrics") +
  density_theme
```

# Pace and shape:

## Female demographic pPCA

The variation in life history traits among animals is evident across eight traits. As predicted by the fast–slow continuum, time-dependent traits like median and maximum lifespan, life expectancy at eclosion, and reproductive maturity are positively correlated (Fig. 3). These traits form one axis of variation in life history strategies, accounting for 46% of the variation in the analysis of 148 species. Along this axis, species range from short-lived early reproducers, such as D. persimillis and D. rhopaloa, to long-lived, slow-maturing species like D. bifurca. However, contrary to the prediction, long-lived species also produced more offspring.

)

### Make data

```{r}

fun_phylomorphospace <- function(data, col_name) {
  X1 = data %>% select(dry_mass, {{ col_name }}, Broad_clade)
  obj1 <- phylomorphospace(combo_phylo_demo_log$phy, X = X1 %>% select(-c(Broad_clade)))
  df1 <- data.frame(
    xstart = obj1$xx[obj1$edge[, 1]],
    ystart = obj1$yy[obj1$edge[, 1]],
    xstop = obj1$xx[obj1$edge[, 2]],
    ystop = obj1$yy[obj1$edge[, 2]],
    nodestart = obj1$edge[, 1],
    nodestop = obj1$edge[, 2]
  )
  p <- ggplot() + 
    geom_point(data = X1, aes(x = dry_mass, y = {{ col_name }}), size =
                 1, color = "grey50") +
    geom_smooth(data = X1, aes(x = dry_mass, y = {{ col_name }}), method = "lm", color = "black")+
    scale_x_continuous("log(dry mass)") +
    #scale_color_npg(name = "")+
    #geom_segment(data=df1,aes(x=xstart,y=ystart,xend=xstop,yend=ystop), size = 0.1,color="black")+
    theme_classic2(base_size = 10)
  return(p)
}

## Run PGLS


```{r}

caper_allometry_f <- comparative.data(phy = combo_phylo_demo_log$phy, data = df_allometry_f%>% select(-c(Broad_clade,tot.dry.mass.f,PC1,PC2))%>% rownames_to_column("Species"), names.col = Species)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
df_allo_fit_f<- data.frame()
for(i in colnames(caper_allometry_f$data)[-7]){
  model_formula <- as.formula(paste0(i," ~ dry_mass"))
  print(model_formula)
  pgls_model <- pgls(model_formula, data = caper_allometry_f, lambda = "ML")

model_summary <- summary(pgls_model)

df_allo_fit_f<- bind_rows(df_allo_fit_f, bind_cols( adj.r.squared = model_summary$adj.r.squared, P = model_summary$coefficients["dry_mass", "Pr(>|t|)"]%>%round(3), slope = model_summary$coefficients ["dry_mass", "Estimate" ] )%>% mutate(Trait = i))
}
df_allo_fit_f%>%clipr::write_clip()


caper_allometry_m <- comparative.data(phy = combo_phylo_demo_log$phy, data = df_allometry_m%>% select(-c(Broad_clade,tot.dry.mass.m))%>% rownames_to_column("Species"), names.col = Species)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
df_allo_fit_m<- data.frame()
for(i in colnames(caper_allometry_m$data)[-7]){
  model_formula <- as.formula(paste0(i," ~ dry_mass"))
  print(model_formula)
  pgls_model <- pgls(model_formula, data = caper_allometry_m, lambda = "ML")

model_summary <- summary(pgls_model)

df_allo_fit_m<- bind_rows(df_allo_fit_m, bind_cols( adj.r.squared = model_summary$adj.r.squared, P = model_summary$coefficients["dry_mass", "Pr(>|t|)"]%>%round(10), slope = model_summary$coefficients ["dry_mass", "Estimate" ] )%>% mutate(Trait = i))
}
df_allo_fit_m%>%clipr::write_clip()

}

```{r}
array_lifespan_m <- combo_phylo_demo_log$data%>%

## Bivariate using pgls

### Make caper data
```{r}
multi_inner_join <- function(dataframes, by){
  reduce(dataframes, inner_join, by = by)
}

df_combined <- list(
  df_species_metadata %>%
    dplyr::select(Species, Broad_clade),
  combo_phylo_demo_log$data %>%
    rownames_to_column("Species")%>%
    mutate(across(starts_with("e0_"),.fns = ~ exp(.))),
  #df_pPCA_demo_m%>%select(Species, shape_m = PC1, pace_m =PC2),
  #df_pPCA_demo_f%>%select(Species, shape_f = PC1, pace_f =PC2),
  df_non_demo_data
) %>%
  multi_inner_join(by = "Species")%>%
  dplyr::select(-ends_with("_se"))

# combine with tree
combo_phylo_full <- match.phylo.data(
  phy = combo_phylo_demo_log$phy, 
  data = df_combined%>%
    select(-c(Broad_clade))%>%
    column_to_rownames("Species"))
combo_phylo_full$data<- combo_phylo_full$data%>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ as.numeric(.)))
# maker comparative for pgls
caper_full <- comparative.data(
  phy = combo_phylo_full$phy,
  data = combo_phylo_full$data %>%
    # mutate(repro_maturity_f = factor(repro_maturity_f),
    #        repro_maturity_m = factor(repro_maturity_m))%>%
    rownames_to_column("Species"),
  names.col = "Species",
  vcv = T,na.omit = F,
  vcv.dim = 3,
  warn.dropped = T
)

### Plotting fun
```{r}
fun_phylomorphospace2 <- function(caperData, col_name1, col_name2, slope1, intercept1,slope_repl,intercept_repl ){
  X1 = caperData$data %>%
    rownames_to_column("Species") %>%
    left_join(df_pcametadata %>%
                select(Species, Broad_clade), by = "Species") %>%
    mutate({{ col_name1 }} := log({{ col_name1 }}), Clade = case_when(Broad_clade == "Repleta" ~ "Repleta", .default =  NA)) %>%
    
    select({{ col_name1 }}, {{ col_name2 }}, Clade)
    
#   obj1<- phylomorphospace(caperData$phy, X = X1)
#   df1<-data.frame(
# 	xstart=obj1$xx[obj1$edge[,1]],
# 	ystart=obj1$yy[obj1$edge[,1]],
# 	xstop=obj1$xx[obj1$edge[,2]],
# 	ystop=obj1$yy[obj1$edge[,2]],
# 	nodestart=obj1$edge[,1],
# 	nodestop=obj1$edge[,2])
  p<- ggplot(data=X1,aes(x = ({{ col_name1 }}),y=({{ col_name2 }}), color = Clade ))+
    geom_point(size=1)+
    geom_abline(slope = slope1, intercept = intercept1,
                color = "black",
                linewidth = 0.8)+
    geom_abline(slope = slope_repl, intercept = intercept_repl,
                color = "#DC0000FF",
                linewidth = 0.8)+
    scale_color_npg(name = "",na.value = "grey50" )+
    #geom_segment(data=df1,aes(x=xstart,y=ystart,xend=xstop,yend=ystop), size = 0.1,color="black")+
    theme_classic2(base_size = 12 )+
    theme(axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  return(p)
}

### Only repleta species

```{r}
combo_phylo_repleta <- match.phylo.data(phy = combo_phylo_full$phy, 
                                           data = df_combined%>%
                                             filter(Broad_clade %in% c( "Repleta"))%>%
                                             select(-c(Broad_clade))%>%
                                             ungroup()%>%
                                             filter(sp.total.len>0 )%>%
                                             column_to_rownames("Species"))
combo_phylo_repleta$data<- combo_phylo_repleta$data%>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ as.numeric(.)))


caper_repleta <- comparative.data(phy = combo_phylo_repleta$phy,
                                           data = combo_phylo_repleta$data%>% rownames_to_column("Species"),
                                           names.col = Species, vcv = T, vcv.dim = 3, na.omit = F,
                                           warn.dropped = T
                                           )

### pANCOVA Repleta with subgroup

#### Make data

```{r}

mulleri_subgroup <- df_species_metadata$Species[which(df_species_metadata$subgroup == "mulleri")]

hydei_subgroup <- df_species_metadata$Species[which(df_species_metadata$subgroup == "hydei")]

repleta_subgroup <- df_species_metadata$Species[which(df_species_metadata$subgroup == "repleta")]

mercatorum_subgroup <- df_species_metadata$Species[which(df_species_metadata$subgroup == "mercatorum")]   


df_pANOVA<- df_combined%>%
  select(Species,e0_m,e0_f, H_m,H_f,std_aging_rate_f,std_aging_rate_m, tot.dry.mass.m,tot.dry.mass.f, sp.total.len, sr.len, Broad_clade)%>%
  mutate(Repleta_bin = case_when(Broad_clade == "Repleta" ~ "Y", .default = "N"),
         Repleta_bin = factor(Repleta_bin),
         repleta_subgroup =case_when(Species %in% mulleri_subgroup ~ "mulleri_subgroup",
                                     Species %in% hydei_subgroup ~ "hydei_subgroup",
                                     Species %in% repleta_subgroup ~ "repleta_subgroup",
                                     Species %in% mercatorum_subgroup ~ "mercatorum_subgroup",
                                     .default = "Non-repleta"),
         repleta_subgroup = factor(repleta_subgroup, levels =c("Non-repleta","hydei_subgroup", "mercatorum_subgroup","mulleri_subgroup", "repleta_subgroup" )),
         hydei_bin = case_when(
                                     Species %in% hydei_subgroup ~ "Y",
                                     .default = "N"),
         hydei_bin = factor(hydei_bin))%>%
           column_to_rownames("Species")
  
spp<-rownames(df_pANOVA)

df_pANOVA%>%
  select(hydei_bin)%>%
  rownames_to_column("Species")%>%
  left_join(caper_full$data%>%rownames_to_column("Species"), by = "Species")%>%view()

```

#### Male

##e0 vs spl

corPagel<-corPagel(0.1, phy = combo_phylo_demo_log$phy, form = ~ spp)

# Ancova with repleta binary

fit_ancova_rep_bin<- gls(e0_m ~ log(tot.dry.mass.m) + log(sp.total.len)*Repleta_bin,
                        data=df_pANOVA,
                        correlation=corPagel)

glht_ancova_rep_bin<-glht(fit_ancova_rep_bin,linfct=mcp(Repleta_bin="Tukey"))

fit_ancova_rep_sg<- gls(e0_m ~ log(tot.dry.mass.m) + log(sp.total.len)*repleta_subgroup,
                        data=df_pANOVA,
                        correlation=corPagel)
anova(fit_ancova_rep_sg, fit_ancova_rep_bin_red)




glht_ancova_rep_sg<-glht(fit_ancova_rep_sg,linfct=mcp(repleta_subgroup="Tukey"))



fit_ancova_hyd_bin<- gls(e0_m ~ log(tot.dry.mass.m) + log(sp.total.len)*hydei_bin,
                        data=df_pANOVA,
                        correlation=corPagel)
